newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - May 14.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The ACT rugby union Brumbies may see their Super 12 semi-final side ripped apart by provincial poachers unless they receive an increase in funds from the Australian Rugby Union. Many key players are due to come off contract at the end of this season, with many already targeted by series rivals. Page 40.

Australian Football League team Carlton yesterday claimed a nine-match suspension, handed down to player Greg Williams after he was charged with unduly interfering with an umpire, had the potential to see the team miss out on a $1.5 million windfall in revenue. Page 40.

Australian hockey player Rachel Imison was yesterday promoted to the national women's hockey team for the six-nation Champions Trophy tournament. The 18-year-old only became a specialist goal-keeper last year, and was not part of the 28-member senior squad selected earlier this year. Page 39.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

This weekend will for the first time in memory, see the ABC broadcast a national league soccer match on Sydney's 2BL radio's Sunday Grandstand program. The move sees soccer as an unexpected beneficiary in the radio war involving the ABC and the Australia Rugby League. Page 46.

Australian brewer Tooheys will return to its position as long-term sponsor of the New South Wales rugby league team in a move prompted by a settlement on the steps of the NSW Supreme Court between the NSW Rugby League and sports drink company Gatorade. Ealier this year Tooheys, the NSW and State of Origin sponsor, announced it would sever all ties with the NSWRL. Page 46.

Australian Paralympic sprint champion Amy Winters, born with only half her right arm, has pioneered the use of a tripod which supports her arm stump and provides a level and faster start. The invention helped Winters win a 200 metre event gold medal in wold -record time at last year's Atlanta Paralympic Games. Page 45.
THE AGE

Victorian cricket will soon see dramatic changes to district competition as well as a change in policy that will release selectors to chase interstate players. The moves come after Monday night's change of the articles of association to allow Victoria to boost its playing stocks, and in the lead up to a paper suggesting wide-ranging changes to club cricket. Page B16.

Australian tennis player Mark Philippoussis suffered a 6-2, 6-0 defeat against Moroccan Karim Alami in the Italian Open championship in Rome yesterday. The early exit strikes a blow to Philippousis' French Open preparation, now only two weeks away, with the player saying he was not mentally prepared for the match. Page B14.

Australian motorcycle champion Michael Doohan is looking forward to Sunday's Italian Grand Prix despite the growing threat from arch-rival and teammate Alex Criville in the 500cc motorcycle world championship. Doohan has been unbeaten on the Italian Mugelo circuit since he won the 1993 San Marino Grand Prix. Page B14.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian swimmer Susie Maroney has attributed her success of her Cuba to Florida swim to months of training, a lot of determination, and a trick played by her brother enabling her to get a full night's sleep before the swim. Maroney began swimming as a child to combat her asthma. Page 78.

Australian cricket player Shane Warne is considering playing English county cricket next summer, much to the dismay of the Australian Cricket Board. Warne was offered a deal worth a rumoured several hundred thousand dollars by club Worcestershire for a single season several years ago. Page 77.

The future of Australian basketball player Mark Bradtke's international career could be decided on Monday when Bradtke and national head coach Barry Barnes meet before the Australia-Croatia match in Melbourne. Bradtke did not arrive at a Canberra training camp this week, citing a virus. Page 72.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian businessman Syd Fischer has announced he will challenge for the yachting America's Cup in 2000 in either a new international class design or a revamped version of his 1995 boat. The move means Fischer will have campaigned five times for the Cup in the world's oldest sporting competition. Page 80.

Australian Socceroo and Sydney United goalkeeper Zeljko Kalac said yesterday that if his teammates wanted to play an individual sport they would be better off playing tennis. Kalac is disappointed the Ericsson Cup grand final will not be played in Sydney.Page 80.

Australian racehorse trainer Gai Waterhouse believes jockey Shane Dye can maintain his winter carnival momentum when he rides Stony Bay in the 2,400 metre A$300,000 Prime Minister's Cup at the Gold Coast today. Page 83.
